transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

Thank you, that's reassuring. I've tried those checks. The brush bar is clean, the wand is clear, and I washed the filter last month and let it dry for a full day. The screen says 'Auto', which I switched to from Eco about two weeks ago. In Eco it stays the same quiet sound on both the rug and the tiles, and in Boost it's loud all the time. There's no heat, burning smell, sparks or warning lights. Is Auto meant to change the power like this?

Yes. That is exactly what Auto mode is designed to do.

On the Dyson V15 Detect, Auto mode adjusts suction power automatically according to the resistance/load at the cleaner head and, with compatible heads, the amount of dust being detected. A rug creates more resistance than smooth kitchen tile, so the vacuum increases power: it sounds louder and the LCD’s predicted remaining run time drops more quickly. Back on tile, it reduces power again.

Your comparison is a good confirmation:

• Eco: low, fixed power, so similar sound on tile and rug.
• Boost: high, fixed power, so loud on both surfaces.
• Auto: variable power, so it changes as you move between surfaces.

The display changing is also expected. The minutes shown are a live estimate, not a fixed battery percentage: if Auto raises the motor power, it recalculates to fewer minutes remaining; when demand reduces, the estimate may settle or increase.

Given that it is only four months old, has no warnings, overheating, odd smells, loss of suction, or cutting out, and behaves consistently in Eco/Boost, there is no indication from this that the motor is failing.
